import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture

The Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture asks whether every $4$-vertex-connected toroidal graph
has a Hamiltonian cycle. It generalises Tutte's theorem that every $4$-vertex-connected planar
graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.

A graph is *toroidal* if it can be drawn on the torus without crossings. Mathlib has no notion
of a graph embedded in a surface, so this file defines `EmbedsIn G X`: the vertices of `G` are
represented by distinct points of the topological space `X` and the edges by simple arcs, such
that arcs meet only at common endpoints and pass through no other vertex. This is the standard
topological definition of an embedding (see e.g. Mohar–Thomassen, *Graphs on Surfaces*, §2.1).
The torus is the product $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ of two circles.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gr%C3%BCnbaum%E2%80%93Nash-Williams_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Toroidal graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toroidal_graph)
- [TY97] Thomas, R. and Yu, X., *Five-connected toroidal graphs are Hamiltonian*,
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 69 (1997), 79–96.
- [TYZ05] Thomas, R., Yu, X. and Zang, W., *Hamilton paths in toroidal graphs*,
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 94 (2005), 214–236.
- [Tu56] Tutte, W. T., *A theorem on planar graphs*, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 82 (1956), 99–116.
-/

namespace GrunbaumNashWilliamsConjecture

open SimpleGraph
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/-- The torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = S^1 \times S^1$, realised as the product of two copies of the
circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. -/
abbrev Torus : Type := UnitAddCircle × UnitAddCircle

/-- A simple graph `G` *embeds* in a topological space `X` if there are
* an injective map `f` sending vertices to points of `X`, and
* for each edge `e`, a simple arc `γ e` in `X` (a continuous injective map from $[0,1]$)
  whose endpoints are the images of the two endpoints of `e`,

such that an arc passes through the image of a vertex only at its own endpoints, and two
distinct arcs meet only at images of vertices (hence only at common endpoints). -/
def EmbedsIn {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : V → X) (γ : G.edgeSet → C(unitInterval, X)),
    Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ e, Function.Injective (γ e)) ∧
    (∀ e : G.edgeSet, Sym2.map f e = s(γ e 0, γ e 1)) ∧
    (∀ (e : G.edgeSet) (v : V), f v ∈ Set.range (γ e) → v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)) ∧
    (∀ e e' : G.edgeSet, e ≠ e' → Set.range (γ e) ∩ Set.range (γ e') ⊆ Set.range f)

/-- A graph is *toroidal* if it embeds in the torus. Every planar graph is toroidal, see
`IsPlanar.isToroidal`. -/
def IsToroidal {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  EmbedsIn G Torus

/-- A graph is *planar* if it embeds in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. -/
def IsPlanar {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  EmbedsIn G ℝ²

/-- If `G` embeds in `X` then so does every subgraph of `G` on the same vertex set. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem EmbedsIn.anti {V : Type*} {G H : SimpleGraph V} {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (hHG : H ≤ G) (hG : EmbedsIn G X) : EmbedsIn H X := by
  obtain ⟨f, γ, hf, hγ, hends, hvert, hdisj⟩ := hG
  refine ⟨f, fun e => γ ⟨e, edgeSet_mono hHG e.2⟩, hf, fun e => hγ _,
    fun e => hends ⟨e, edgeSet_mono hHG e.2⟩,
    fun e v hv => hvert _ v hv, fun e e' hee' => hdisj _ _ fun h => hee' ?_⟩
  exact Subtype.ext congr(($h).1)

/-- An embedding in `X` composed with a continuous injection `X → Y` is an embedding in `Y`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem EmbedsIn.of_injective_continuous {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V}
    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (hG : EmbedsIn G X)
    {φ : X → Y} (hφ : Function.Injective φ) (hφc : Continuous φ) : EmbedsIn G Y := by
  obtain ⟨f, γ, hf, hγ, hends, hvert, hdisj⟩ := hG
  refine ⟨φ ∘ f, fun e => (⟨φ, hφc⟩ : C(X, Y)).comp (γ e), hφ.comp hf,
    fun e => hφ.comp (hγ e), fun e => ?_, fun e v ⟨t, ht⟩ => hvert e v ⟨t, hφ ht⟩,
    fun e e' hee' y ⟨⟨t, ht⟩, ⟨t', ht'⟩⟩ => ?_⟩
  · rw [← Sym2.map_map, hends e, Sym2.map_pair_eq]
    rfl
  · obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := hdisj e e' hee' ⟨⟨t, hφ (ht.trans ht'.symm)⟩, ⟨t', rfl⟩⟩
    exact ⟨v, (congrArg φ hv).trans ht'⟩

/-- Every planar graph is toroidal: the plane embeds in the torus. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsPlanar.isToroidal {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} (hG : IsPlanar G) : IsToroidal G := by
  -- `g` is a continuous injection `ℝ → (0, 1)`, and `(↑)` is injective on `[0, 1)`.
  let g : ℝ → ℝ := fun x => 1 / 2 + Real.arctan x / Real.pi
  have hg : ∀ x, g x ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (0 + 1) := fun x => by
    have h1 := Real.arctan_lt_pi_div_two x
    have h2 := Real.neg_pi_div_two_lt_arctan x
    have hpi := Real.pi_pos
    simp only [g, Set.mem_Ico, zero_add]
    constructor
    · have : -(1 / 2 : ℝ) < Real.arctan x / Real.pi := by
        rw [lt_div_iff₀ hpi]; linarith
      linarith
    · have : Real.arctan x / Real.pi < 1 / 2 := by
        rw [div_lt_iff₀ hpi]; linarith
      linarith
  have hginj : Function.Injective g := fun x y hxy => by
    simpa [g, Real.pi_ne_zero] using hxy
  have hgc : Continuous g := by fun_prop
  let φ : ℝ² → Torus := fun p => ((g (p 0) : UnitAddCircle), (g (p 1) : UnitAddCircle))
  refine hG.of_injective_continuous (φ := φ) (fun p q hpq => ?_) (by fun_prop)
  simp only [φ, Prod.mk.injEq, AddCircle.coe_eq_coe_iff_of_mem_Ico (hg _) (hg _)] at hpq
  ext i
  fin_cases i
  · exact hginj hpq.1
  · exact hginj hpq.2

/-- A single edge is planar: the definition of `EmbedsIn` is satisfiable. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isPlanar_top_fin_two : IsPlanar (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) := by
  let p : ℝ² := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1
  have hp : p ≠ 0 := by
    simp [p]
  have hedge : ∀ e : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).edgeSet, (e : Sym2 (Fin 2)) = s(0, 1) := by
    rintro ⟨e, he⟩
    induction e using Sym2.ind with
    | _ a b =>
      rw [mem_edgeSet, top_adj] at he
      fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> simp_all [Sym2.eq_swap]
  refine ⟨fun i => ((i : ℕ) : ℝ) • p, fun _ => ⟨fun t => (t : ℝ) • p, by fun_prop⟩,
    fun i j hij => ?_, fun e s t hst => ?_, fun e => ?_, fun e v _ => ?_, fun e e' hee' => ?_⟩
  · exact Fin.val_injective (Nat.cast_injective (smul_left_injective ℝ hp hij))
  · exact Subtype.val_injective (smul_left_injective ℝ hp hst)
  · rw [hedge e, Sym2.map_pair_eq]
    simp
  · rw [hedge e]
    fin_cases v <;> simp
  · exact absurd (Subtype.ext ((hedge e).trans (hedge e').symm)) hee'

/-- A single edge is toroidal. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isToroidal_top_fin_two : IsToroidal (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) :=
  isPlanar_top_fin_two.isToroidal

/--
**Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture.**
Does every $4$-vertex-connected toroidal graph have a Hamiltonian cycle?

Here a graph is $4$-vertex-connected if it has more than $4$ vertices and remains connected
after the removal of any set of fewer than $4$ vertices (`IsKConnected G 4`), and it is toroidal
if it can be drawn on the torus without crossings (`IsToroidal`); planar graphs are included.
The conjectured answer is yes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem grunbaum_nash_williams_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      IsToroidal G → IsKConnected G 4 → G.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

/--
**Tutte's theorem.** Every $4$-vertex-connected planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. The
Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture generalises this from the plane to the torus.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem grunbaum_nash_williams_conjecture.variants.planar (V : Type) [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : IsPlanar G) (h4 : IsKConnected G 4) :
    G.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

/--
**Thomas–Yu (1997).** Every $5$-vertex-connected toroidal graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem grunbaum_nash_williams_conjecture.variants.five_connected (V : Type) [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : IsToroidal G) (h5 : IsKConnected G 5) :
    G.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

/--
**Thomas–Yu–Zang (2005).** Every $4$-vertex-connected toroidal graph has a Hamiltonian path,
i.e. a walk visiting every vertex exactly once.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem grunbaum_nash_williams_conjecture.variants.hamiltonian_path (V : Type) [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : IsToroidal G) (h4 : IsKConnected G 4) :
    ∃ (a b : V) (p : G.Walk a b), p.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

end GrunbaumNashWilliamsConjecture

modeling_decisions: The list-page entry is phrased as a question ('whether ...'), so the slot uses `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ...`; `answer(True)` is the conjectured positive answer.

'Toroidal graph' is formalized by the standard topological definition (embeddable in the torus without crossings) via bespoke `EmbedsIn`; the torus is `UnitAddCircle × UnitAddCircle`. Planar graphs are therefore toroidal, which is proved (not sorried) as `IsPlanar.isToroidal` using an explicit continuous injection ℝ² → torus.

Arcs are indexed by `G.edgeSet` (unordered pairs) with endpoint condition `Sym2.map f e = s(γ e 0, γ e 1)`, avoiding the need for a consistency condition between `arc u v` and `arc v u`. Arcs are continuous injective maps from `unitInterval`; in Hausdorff spaces (torus, plane) these are exactly simple arcs.

Graphs are finite simple graphs (`SimpleGraph V`, `[Fintype V]`, `V : Type`). Loops/multi-edges are irrelevant to Hamiltonicity and connectivity, and every finite graph is isomorphic to one with vertex type in `Type`, so nothing is lost. `[DecidableEq V]` is required by Mathlib's `IsHamiltonian`.

namespace GrunbaumNashWilliamsConjecture

/-- A simple graph is toroidal if it has a crossing-free topological drawing in the torus
`Circle × Circle`. Vertices are represented by distinct points and edges by embedded arcs. Each
arc has its incident vertices as endpoints, contains no other vertex, and meets another arc only at
a common endpoint. This means embeddability in the torus (orientable genus at most one), so planar
graphs are included. -/
def IsToroidal {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (vertex : V → Circle × Circle)
    (edge : G.edgeSet → unitInterval → Circle × Circle),
    Function.Injective vertex ∧
      (∀ e, Topology.IsEmbedding (edge e)) ∧
      (∀ e, edge e '' ({0, 1} : Set unitInterval) =
        vertex '' {v | v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)}) ∧
      (∀ e t v, edge e t = vertex v → t = 0 ∨ t = 1) ∧
      ∀ e f, e ≠ f → ∀ s t, edge e s = edge f t →
        ∃ v, v ∈ (e : Sym2 V) ∧ v ∈ (f : Sym2 V) ∧ edge e s = vertex v

/--
**Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture**

Every finite simple graph that is 4-vertex-connected and embeddable in the torus has a Hamiltonian
cycle. Here 4-vertex-connected graphs have at least five vertices.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]

    ∀ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      letI := Classical.decEq V
      G.IsKConnected 4 → IsToroidal G → G.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

end GrunbaumNashWilliamsConjecture

/-!
# Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture

The Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture states that every $4$-vertex-connected toroidal graph has
a Hamiltonian cycle. It generalises Tutte's theorem that every $4$-vertex-connected planar graph
has a Hamiltonian cycle. The conjecture was formulated in the early 1970s by Branko Grünbaum and
Crispin Nash-Williams.

Partial progress: Thomas and Yu proved that every $5$-vertex-connected toroidal graph has a
Hamiltonian cycle, and Thomas, Yu and Zang proved that every $4$-vertex-connected toroidal graph
has a Hamiltonian path.

A *toroidal graph* is a graph that can be embedded in the torus. Mathlib has no notion of a graph
embedded in a surface, so this file defines topological graph embeddings directly. An embedding of
a simple graph in a topological space `X` places the vertices injectively in `X` and draws every
edge as a simple arc joining the images of its endpoints, such that the interiors of the arcs
contain no vertex and are pairwise disjoint.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gr%C3%BCnbaum%E2%80%93Nash-Williams_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Toroidal graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toroidal_graph)
- [TY97] R. Thomas, X. Yu, *Five-connected toroidal graphs are Hamiltonian*,
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 69 (1997), 79–96.
- [TYZ05] R. Thomas, X. Yu, W. Zang, *Hamilton paths in toroidal graphs*,
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 94 (2005), 214–236.
-/

namespace GrunbaumNashWilliamsConjecture

open SimpleGraph unitInterval

variable {V : Type*}

/-- The torus $\mathbb{R}^2 / \mathbb{Z}^2$, as the product of two circles. -/
abbrev Torus : Type := UnitAddCircle × UnitAddCircle

/-- A (topological) embedding of the simple graph `G` in the topological space `X`. The vertices of
`G` are placed injectively in `X`, and every edge `e` of `G` is drawn as a simple arc `arc e`
joining the images of the two endpoints of `e`. The interior of an arc contains no vertex, and the
interiors of the arcs of two distinct edges are disjoint. -/
structure GraphEmbedding (G : SimpleGraph V) (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] where
  /-- The position of each vertex. -/
  vertex : V → X
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  /-- The arc drawing each edge, parametrised by the unit interval. -/
  arc : G.edgeSet → I → X
  arc_continuous (e : G.edgeSet) : Continuous (arc e)
  arc_injective (e : G.edgeSet) : Function.Injective (arc e)
  /-- The arc of the edge `e` joins the images of the two endpoints of `e`. -/
  arc_endpoints (e : G.edgeSet) : s(arc e 0, arc e 1) = Sym2.map vertex e
  /-- The interior of an arc contains no vertex. -/
  arc_interior_not_mem_range_vertex (e : G.edgeSet) (t : I) (ht : t ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) :
    arc e t ∉ Set.range vertex
  /-- The interiors of the arcs of two distinct edges are disjoint. -/
  arc_interior_disjoint :
    Pairwise fun e e' : G.edgeSet ↦ Disjoint (arc e '' Set.Ioo 0 1) (arc e' '' Set.Ioo 0 1)

/-- A simple graph is *toroidal* if it can be embedded in the torus. -/
def IsToroidal (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop := Nonempty (GraphEmbedding G Torus)

/-- An embedding of `G` restricts to an embedding of every graph `H ≤ G` on the same vertices. -/
def GraphEmbedding.ofLE {G H : SimpleGraph V} {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (hHG : H ≤ G) (φ : GraphEmbedding G X) : GraphEmbedding H X where
  vertex := φ.vertex
  vertex_injective := φ.vertex_injective
  arc e := φ.arc (Set.inclusion (edgeSet_mono hHG) e)
  arc_continuous _ := φ.arc_continuous _
  arc_injective _ := φ.arc_injective _
  arc_endpoints _ := φ.arc_endpoints _
  arc_interior_not_mem_range_vertex _ := φ.arc_interior_not_mem_range_vertex _
  arc_interior_disjoint _ _ hee' :=
    φ.arc_interior_disjoint (Set.inclusion_injective _ |>.ne hee')

/-- Every graph `H ≤ G` on the same vertices as a toroidal graph `G` is toroidal. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsToroidal.mono {G H : SimpleGraph V} (hHG : H ≤ G) (hG : IsToroidal G) :
    IsToroidal H :=
  hG.map (GraphEmbedding.ofLE hHG)

# Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture

The Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture states that every 4-vertex-connected toroidal graph
has a Hamiltonian cycle. It generalises Tutte's theorem that every 4-vertex-connected planar
graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.

A graph is *toroidal* if it can be drawn without crossings on the torus. Mathlib has no notion
of graph embeddings in surfaces, so this file defines a topological embedding of a simple graph
in a topological space: vertices go to distinct points, every edge is realised by an arc joining
the images of its endpoints, and arcs meet only at vertices. Toroidal graphs are the graphs with
such an embedding in the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.

- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gr%C3%BCnbaum%E2%80%93Nash-Williams_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics]

- [Gr70] Grünbaum, B., *Polytopes, graphs, and complexes*. Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 76 (1970),
  1131–1201.
- [NW73] Nash-Williams, C. St. J. A., *Unexplored and semi-explored territories in graph theory*.
  In: New directions in the theory of graphs (Proc. Third Ann Arbor Conf.), Academic Press (1973),
  149–186.
- [Tu56] Tutte, W. T., *A theorem on planar graphs*. Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 82 (1956), 99–116.
- [TY97] Thomas, R. and Yu, X., *Five-connected toroidal graphs are Hamiltonian*.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 69 (1997), 79–96.
- [TYZ05] Thomas, R., Yu, X. and Zang, W., *Hamilton paths in toroidal graphs*.

-/

variable {V : Type*}

/-- A topological embedding (a drawing without crossings) of the simple graph `G` in the
topological space `X`. The vertices are sent to distinct points of `X`. Every edge `e` is realised
by an arc `arc e`, a homeomorphic copy of the unit interval `I` in `X`, whose two endpoints are
the images of the two endpoints of `e`. No arc passes through the image of a vertex in its
interior, and two distinct arcs meet only at images of vertices, hence only at common endpoints. -/
structure TopologicalEmbedding (G : SimpleGraph V) (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] where
  /-- The point of `X` representing a vertex. -/
  vertex : V → X
  vertex_injective : Function.Injective vertex
  /-- The arc of `X` representing an edge, parametrised by the unit interval. -/
  arc : G.edgeSet → I → X
  arc_isEmbedding : ∀ e, IsEmbedding (arc e)
  arc_endpoints : ∀ e : G.edgeSet, Sym2.map vertex e = s(arc e 0, arc e 1)
  arc_interior : ∀ e t, t ≠ 0 → t ≠ 1 → arc e t ∉ Set.range vertex
  arc_inter : ∀ e e', e ≠ e' → Set.range (arc e) ∩ Set.range (arc e') ⊆ Set.range vertex

/-- The torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. -/
local notation "𝕋²" => UnitAddCircle × UnitAddCircle

/-- A simple graph is *toroidal* if it can be drawn without crossings on the torus.
Every planar graph is toroidal. -/
def IsToroidal (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (TopologicalEmbedding G 𝕋²)

/-- A simple graph is *planar* if it can be drawn without crossings in the plane. -/
def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (TopologicalEmbedding G ℝ²)

/-- The graph with one vertex and no edges embeds in every nonempty space. -/

theorem nonempty_topologicalEmbedding_bot_unit (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [Nonempty X] :
    Nonempty (TopologicalEmbedding (⊥ : SimpleGraph Unit) X) :=
  have : IsEmpty (⊥ : SimpleGraph Unit).edgeSet := by rw [edgeSet_bot]; infer_instance
  ⟨{ vertex := fun _ => Classical.arbitrary X
     vertex_injective := fun _ _ _ => rfl
     arc := isEmptyElim
     arc_isEmbedding := isEmptyElim
     arc_endpoints := isEmptyElim
     arc_interior := isEmptyElim
     arc_inter := isEmptyElim }⟩

  nonempty_topologicalEmbedding_bot_unit _

  nonempty_topologicalEmbedding_bot_unit _

/-!
# Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture

The Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture states that every 4-vertex-connected toroidal graph has a
Hamiltonian cycle. It generalises Tutte's theorem that every 4-vertex-connected planar graph has
a Hamiltonian cycle. Thomas and Yu proved that every 5-vertex-connected toroidal graph has a
Hamiltonian cycle, and Thomas, Yu and Zang proved that every 4-vertex-connected toroidal graph
has a Hamiltonian path.

A toroidal graph is a graph that can be embedded in the torus: its vertices are drawn as distinct
points and its edges as simple arcs that meet only at common endpoints. Planar graphs are toroidal.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gr%C3%BCnbaum%E2%80%93Nash-Williams_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Gr70] Grünbaum, B., *Polytopes, graphs, and complexes*, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 76 (1970),
  1131--1201.
- [NW73] Nash-Williams, C. St. J. A., *Unexplored and semi-explored territories in graph theory*,
  in: New directions in the theory of graphs, Academic Press (1973), 149--186.
- [TY97] Thomas, R. and Yu, X., *Five-connected toroidal graphs are Hamiltonian*,
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 69 (1997), 79--96.
- [TYZ05] Thomas, R., Yu, X. and Zang, W., *Hamilton paths in toroidal graphs*,
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 94 (2005), 214--236.
-/

open SimpleGraph unitInterval

namespace GrunbaumNashWilliamsConjecture

variable {V : Type*}

/-- A simple graph `G` is *embeddable* in a topological space `X` if it can be drawn in `X`
without crossings. Concretely, there are an injective map `f` sending vertices to points of `X`
and, for each edge `{u, v}`, a simple arc `γ` in `X` from `f u` to `f v` (the same arc for both
orientations of the edge), such that

* an arc meets the vertex points `f w` only at its two endpoints, and
* the arcs of two distinct edges meet only at vertex points, hence only at common endpoints. -/
def EmbeddableIn (G : SimpleGraph V) (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : V → X) (γ : ∀ ⦃u v⦄, G.Adj u v → Path (f u) (f v)),
    Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ ⦃u v⦄ (h : G.Adj u v), γ h.symm = (γ h).symm) ∧
    (∀ ⦃u v⦄ (h : G.Adj u v), Function.Injective (γ h)) ∧
    (∀ ⦃u v⦄ (h : G.Adj u v) (t : I), γ h t ∈ Set.range f → t = 0 ∨ t = 1) ∧
    (∀ ⦃u v u' v'⦄ (h : G.Adj u v) (h' : G.Adj u' v'), s(u, v) ≠ s(u', v') →
      ∀ t t' : I, γ h t = γ h' t' → γ h t ∈ Set.range f)

/-- A simple graph is *toroidal* if it is embeddable in the torus $S^1 \times S^1$, which we
model as `UnitAddCircle × UnitAddCircle`. Every planar graph is toroidal. -/
def IsToroidal (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  EmbeddableIn G (UnitAddCircle × UnitAddCircle)

/-- Embeddability passes to subgraphs on the same vertex set. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem EmbeddableIn.anti {G H : SimpleGraph V} {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (hHG : H ≤ G) (hG : EmbeddableIn G X) : EmbeddableIn H X := by
  obtain ⟨f, γ, hf, hsymm, hinj, hvert, hdisj⟩ := hG
  exact ⟨f, fun u v h => γ (hHG h), hf, fun u v h => hsymm (hHG h), fun u v h => hinj (hHG h),
    fun u v h => hvert (hHG h), fun u v u' v' h h' => hdisj (hHG h) (hHG h')⟩

/-- The edgeless graph on `V` is embeddable in `X` exactly when `V` injects into `X`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem bot_embeddableIn_iff {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] :
    EmbeddableIn (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) X ↔ ∃ f : V → X, Function.Injective f := by
  refine ⟨fun ⟨f, _, hf, _⟩ => ⟨f, hf⟩, fun ⟨f, hf⟩ => ?_⟩
  exact ⟨f, fun _ _ h => h.elim, hf, fun _ _ h => h.elim, fun _ _ h => h.elim,
    fun _ _ h => h.elim, fun _ _ _ _ h => h.elim⟩

/-- A graph with a single vertex is toroidal. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isToroidal_bot_unit : IsToroidal (⊥ : SimpleGraph Unit) :=
  bot_embeddableIn_iff.mpr ⟨fun _ => 0, fun _ _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩

/-- A toroidal graph stays toroidal after removing edges. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsToroidal.anti {G H : SimpleGraph V} (hHG : H ≤ G) (hG : IsToroidal G) :
    IsToroidal H :=
  EmbeddableIn.anti hHG hG

/--
**Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture.** Is it true that every 4-vertex-connected toroidal graph
has a Hamiltonian cycle?

Here a finite simple graph is 4-vertex-connected if it has more than $4$ vertices and stays
connected after the removal of any set of at most $3$ vertices (`IsKConnected G 4`); this rules
out the degenerate graphs on at most $4$ vertices. Since such a graph has at least $5$ vertices,
`G.IsHamiltonian` says exactly that `G` has a Hamiltonian cycle.

The conjectured answer is yes.
-/

    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      IsKConnected G 4 → IsToroidal G → G.IsHamiltonian := by

**Thomas–Yu (1997).** Every 5-vertex-connected toroidal graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.
-/

    (G : SimpleGraph V) (hG : IsKConnected G 5) (hT : IsToroidal G) : G.IsHamiltonian := by

**Thomas–Yu–Zang (2005).** Every 4-vertex-connected toroidal graph has a Hamiltonian path.
-/
